title.justification: The title of the paper is clearly mentioned at the beginning of both the main document and the supplementary material.

analysis.description: The paper introduces novel random projection techniques, f TT(R) and f CP(R), for high-dimensional tensors using TT and CP decomposition formats respectively. It evaluates their efficiency in preserving Euclidean distances compared to classical Gaussian random projections and presents theoretical analysis and experiments showcasing the superiority of the TT format over CP. The paper also discusses the existence of tensorized random projection maps as Johnson-Lindenstrauss transforms with low memory and computational requirements.

type.justification: The paper supports its claims with experimental results and simulations, which are typical indicators of an empirical study. Specifically, it performs experiments on synthetic data and compares the performance of proposed random projection techniques with conventional methods.
type.quote: Experiments on synthetic data validate our theoretical analysis and demonstrate the superiority of the TT decomposition.

name.justification: The paper primarily focuses on random projection techniques, which are a core aspect of dimensionality reduction in the field of machine learning.
name.quote: Random projections (RP) are commonly used in data science and machine learning to project down high-dimensional data into a lower dimensional space while preserving most of the relevant information in the data.

name.justification: The core focus of the paper is on reducing the dimensionality of high-dimensional tensors using new random projection techniques.
name.quote: We introduce a novel random projection technique for efficiently reducing the dimension of very high-dimensional tensors.

name.justification: The paper heavily uses tensor decomposition techniques such as the TT and CP format to develop its novel random projections.
name.quote: In particular, the CANDECOMP/PARAFAC (CP) [16] and tensor-train (TT) [30] decomposition can represent Nth order d-dimensional tensors...

name.justification: The paper builds its novel tensorized random projection maps on classical results related to Johnson-Lindenstrauss transforms (JLT).
name.quote: Most modern RP techniques build upon the celebrated Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma [20] which shows that an arbitrary number of high-dimensional points can be linearly projected...
